title: Why Color Alone Can Make a Game Unplayable | Game Design

scenes.title: 같은 색을 찾는 순간
lines: In Puyo Puyo Tetris 2, you rotate and move falling Puyos. Connect at least four of one color, and the connected Puyos disappear together.
But if those colors are difficult to tell apart, even choosing what to match becomes difficult. Adding color and communicating clearly are different tasks.
We will reinforce the clues that distinguish colors, keep important objects such as Mario's flowers and paths readable, and use grayscale to check what attracts our attention.

scenes.title: 색 하나에 맡긴 정보
lines: First, reduce only the color difference between these illustrated blocks. If their shapes and patterns are identical, the clue that they are different types disappears with it.
If a theme changes the colors of the blocks and background, checking only the first pair of colors is not enough. The same information must remain readable in every combination that appears.

scenes.title: 시뮬레이션으로 찾는 문제
lines: This is where color-vision simulation helps. It lets us preview whether blocks remain distinct from one another and from the background when certain color differences are reduced.
Photoshop's color-proofing options include Protanopia-type and Deuteranopia-type simulations. They model different color-vision conditions, so we check more than one.

Puyo Puyo Tetris 2 also added color-adjustment options with filters for different color-vision conditions. Developers can test in advance and give players useful choices for distinguishing the information.

scenes.title: 밝기와 모양을 함께
lines: When a problem appears, adjust more than the hue: increase the difference between light and dark as well. A remaining lightness difference can make the boundary easier to find.
Making a block darker without checking its surroundings can hide it against a dark background. We need both distinct block types and separation from the background.
Add another clue, such as a circle, triangle, or stripe pattern. Repeat the same shape for the same type, so color and shape communicate the same information together.

scenes.title: 꽃과 장치를 읽는 방법
lines: The same principle matters outside puzzle games. In Super Mario Bros. Wonder, flowers and question-mark blocks differ in outline and symbols as well as color.
Players learn their roles by touching flowers and hitting blocks. Connecting a visible clue with its actual result gives players several ways to recognize an item or mechanism.

scenes.title: 색을 빼면 보이는 위계
lines: Once we can identify an object, where we look first also matters. Turn the same game image into grayscale. Without vivid hues, the arrangement of light and dark becomes clearer.
What draws your eye first: Mario's path, the next obstacle, or the scenery behind them? A background that dominates the route ahead can pull attention away from play.
Reduce background contrast or strengthen an important boundary to guide the eye through the decisions the player needs to make. This is a way to examine the image's visual hierarchy.

scenes.title: 검사는 서로 다른 질문
lines: Color-vision simulation tests whether color-dependent information survives; grayscale checks lightness and the order of attention. They answer different questions, so we use both.

Flipping artwork can reveal awkward details hidden by familiarity. Temporarily removing color is another way to see an image afresh. Then complement those previews with players who have different color vision.

scenes.title: 전달되는 정보를 남기기
lines: Returning to our puzzle, the goal is more than beautiful colors. Players must recognize matching types, separate them from the background, and choose an action. Color should be one of several clues carrying that information.
